title: Module 2 · Lesson 3 — The framework landscape and NeMo Agent Toolkit

lines: Lesson three maps the agent frameworks and NVIDIA's NeMo Agent Toolkit.
The exam asks which tool fits a need, not how to write it from memory.

say.0: Lesson three maps the agent frameworks and Nvidia's NeMo Agent Toolkit.

lines: Picture a logistics company with three agent teams on three frameworks.
Routing uses LangGraph, customer email uses CrewAI, and invoicing uses AutoGen.
The finance chief asks which agent costs the most per task, and which is most accurate.
Every team measures differently, so nobody can answer.
LangChain brings the broadest integrations, and LlamaIndex centres on retrieval.
CrewAI declares role-based teams, while AutoGen and Semantic Kernel focus on multi-agent conversation.
LangGraph models an agent as a graph over typed state.
Nodes update it, and conditional edges choose what runs next.
A checkpointer saves the state after every node.
So a run can resume after a crash, be replayed for debugging, or pause for human approval.
The step budget lives in the routing function, not in a hopeful prompt.
And an interrupt before tools makes human approval a built-in feature.
NeMo Agent Toolkit, formerly AgentIQ, is NVIDIA's framework-agnostic layer.
It assumes you already have agents, and adds a consistent way to compose, profile, evaluate, and observe them.

say.0: NeMo Agent Toolkit, formerly AgentIQ, is Nvidia's framework-agnostic layer.

lines: In the toolkit, everything is a typed function: tools, model calls, even whole agents.
So one team's entire agent can become a tool for another.
Workflows are wired in YAML, so swapping a model is a config edit, not a code change.
Built-in agent types include ReAct, ReWOO, and router agents.
A profiler attributes tokens, latency, and cost to each step, and an evaluation harness runs datasets in CI.
OpenTelemetry traces flow to Phoenix, Langfuse, or any collector.

lines: It also speaks MCP both ways: it can use MCP servers, and expose its own functions as one.
Now all three logistics agents report cost and accuracy the same way.
A plain loop over an OpenAI-compatible client is fine for a simple, single-purpose agent.
Reach for a framework when you need durable state, branching, human approval, or multi-agent coordination.
On the exam, agents in several frameworks with no consistent measurement points to NeMo Agent Toolkit.
It composes frameworks rather than replacing them, so read on for the full comparison.
